--- title: "Verbal short-term memory" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · HFON_MEMVERB_MEMORIA_VERBAL" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (F · Span and memory; quality class B). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea HFON_MEMVERB_MEMORIA_VERBAL`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Memoria verbal*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/HFON_MEMVERB_MEMORIA_VERBAL.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class B.** It has enough data to be described, but it lacks some of the guarantees of class A (stability across time points, item-level reliability or validity). Use with caution and not for individual decisions. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Verbal short-term memory, from age 4 to 7 (6,939 administrations in 5 cohorts; 2 forms). Stability across time points ρ = .36. AUC .58–.72 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1942 522 | | Battery | DIS-ESP | | Format | forced choice | | Items | 15 (1942); 15 (522) according to the platform | | Task family | F · Span and memory | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | In this task, the child repeats sequences of 1, 2, and 3 CV syllables after been pronounced by the experimenter within one second interval. The response was scored correct when repeated in the same order, disorder if the sequence was altered, but all syllables included; error if at least one syllable was missed. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 28/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:--------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:--------|------------------:| | 1942|Memoria Verbal - CV |Estímulos grabados con auriculares; el niño no ve la pantalla | 15| 0|— |— |fijo |Aciertos | 5, 6, 7| | 522|Memoria Verbal - CV |Un estímulo por pantalla; el evaluador marca acierto o error | 15| 0|— |— |fijo |Aciertos | 4, 4.1, 5, 6| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **1942.** 15 secuencias grabadas (1–5 sílabas), con auriculares. - **522.** 15 secuencias de 1 a 5 sílabas (3 de cada longitud) que lee el evaluador; misma tarea que 1942 pero sin audio. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=2} ![1942 · Memoria Verbal - CV](../../figuras/plataforma/1942.jpg){.lightbox fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 1942"} ![522 · Memoria Verbal - CV](../../figuras/plataforma/522.jpg){.lightbox fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 522"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Repeating sequences of nonsense syllables, from one to five syllables, measures **phonological short-term memory**: keeping in order a series of sounds that are not supported by meaning. It is related to reading because decoding requires holding the sounds of the letters while they are blended. The versions use CV or CVC syllables. **What the evidence says:** - **It adds little beyond phonemic awareness.** A meta-analysis concludes that phonemic awareness is the strongest unique predictor of reading. Longitudinal and experimental studies support its causal role, but not that of verbal short-term memory [@melbylervag2012stm]. In a study from preschool to Grade 3, verbal memory did not predict reading once phonological awareness and RAN were controlled [@parrila2004predictors]. - **Serial order does seem to count at the start.** In 780 children followed from age 4 to 9, serial order memory predicted word reading from age 4 to 6, and reading did not influence it. Pseudoword repetition and reading influenced each other in both directions [@cunningham2021memory]. - **In dyslexia the deficit exists, but it depends on oral language.** Children with dyslexia repeat pseudowords worse than children of their age and than younger readers at the same reading level. Severity varies widely across studies and is explained mainly by oral language level, that is, by co-occurrence with developmental language disorder [@melbylervag2012nonword]. We have not found longitudinal studies in Spanish with this task. **What our data show.** - **Main version (15 items, ages 4 to 7).** α (2021) = .76 and stability across school years ρ = .36 (range .23–.44, about 12 months apart). Its validity grows with age: AUC against persistent difficulty of .58 at age 4, .61 at age 5 and .66–.72 at ages 6–7. Against later low comprehension, .58–.65. The ceiling effect is moderate (4–12%). - **Full version at age 8.** AUC of .63 against persistent difficulty and of .62–.66 against Woodcock-Muñoz. - **CVC version of 1–5 syllables (age 7).** The observed maximum is 3, 86% of children are at ceiling and the AUC is .50. This looks like a recording or scoring error, not a result about the construct: it should not be used until it has been reviewed. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Form| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|----:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.1| 522| 2011| 67|2015/16 | 932| 0| 932| 34| | 4.1| 522| 2012| 154|2016/17 | 389| 389| 0| 17| | 5.1| 522| 2010| 66|2015/16 | 958| 261| 697| 35| | 5.1| 522| 2011| 153|2016/17 | 904| 0| 904| 34| | 5.1| 1942| 2012| 182|2017/18 | 319| 315| 0| 16| | 5.1| 1942| 2014| 896|2019/20 | 354| 13| 341| 21| | 6.1| 522| 2010| 152|2016/17 | 921| 264| 656| 34| | 6.1| 1942| 2011| 183|2017/18 | 764| 0| 764| 31| | 6.2| 1942| 2013| 903|2019/20 | 596| 379| 217| 31| | 7.1| 1942| 2010| 184|2017/18 | 802| 257| 544| 31| | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----:|----------:|---:|----------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 522| 4.1| 389| 2012| 8.97| 3.00| 9| 0.07| 0.00| 4.37| | 1942| 5.1| 328| 2012, 2014| 8.34| 3.31| 8| 0.15| 0.61| 3.66| | 522| 5.1| 261| 2010| 11.28| 2.42| 11| -0.18| 0.00| 12.64| | 522| 6.1| 264| 2010| 11.47| 2.70| 12| -0.83| 0.38| 12.12| | 1942| 6.2| 379| 2013| 10.21| 3.08| 10| -0.36| 0.53| 7.12| | 1942| 7.1| 257| 2010| 11.10| 2.73| 12| -0.50| 0.00| 9.73| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). Internal consistency in the 2021 analyses: α = .76. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|----:| | 2010| 5.1| 6.1| 810| 0.45| 0.44| | 2010| 5.1| 7.1| 664| 0.38| 0.36| | 2010| 6.1| 7.1| 738| 0.41| 0.40| | 2011| 4.1| 5.1| 807| 0.37| 0.36| | 2011| 4.1| 6.1| 637| 0.24| 0.24| | 2011| 5.1| 6.1| 694| 0.29| 0.31| | 2012| 4.1| 5.1| 307| 0.23| 0.23| ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Phonological awareness (4.1, r = .30); Phonological awareness (5.1, r = .35); Phonological awareness (6.1, r = .34); Word and text reading (6.2, r = .35); Phonological awareness (7.1, r = .47). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .58–.72. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .56–.65. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_HFON_MEMVERB_MEMORIA_VERBAL_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .55–.69 (5 time points; 198–585 children). ## Provisional norms | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----:|----------:|---:|----------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 522| 4.1| 389| 2012| 4| 5| 6| 7| 9| 11| 13| | 1942| 5.1| 328| 2012, 2014| 3| 4| 5| 6| 8| 11| 13| | 522| 5.1| 261| 2010| 7| 8| 9| 10| 11| 13| 15| | 1942| 6.1| 764| 2011| 5| 6| 7| 8| 10| 12| 14| | 522| 6.1| 264| 2010| 7| 8| 9| 10| 12| 14| 15| | 1942| 6.2| 379| 2013| 5| 6| 7| 8| 10| 13| 14| | 1942| 7.1| 257| 2010| 6| 7| 8| 9| 12| 13| 14| Each form (platform code) has its own norms, because the forms need not measure on the same scale. These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_HFON_MEMVERB_MEMORIA_VERBAL_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ### Forms: can they be pooled? Forms given at the same time point are compared. They are considered **equivalent** if the mean difference is smaller than 0.20 SD and the SD ratio is between 0.80 and 1.25. If the same children took them, **linear equating** is also computed, which puts the second form on the scale of the first, together with the correlation between forms (parallel-forms reliability). If the groups differ, the difference mixes form and cohort. | Time point| Form 1| Form 2|Comparison | d (2 − 1)| SD ratio|Verdict |r between forms |Equating | |----------:|------:|------:|:----------------|---------:|--------:|:----------------|:---------------|:--------| | 5.1| 1942| 522|different groups | 0.99| 0.73|different scales |— |— | | 6.1| 1942| 522|different groups | 0.62| 0.83|different scales |— |— | ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 4.1| 1,207| -0.040| 0.163| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.1| 1,241| 0.128| 0.024| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.1| 1,233| 0.108| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 4.1| 1,321| 0.306| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.1| 2,460| 0.039| 0.056| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.1| 2,418| 0.047| 0.245| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.1| 2,425| 0.049| 0.015| |School (ICC) | 5.1| 2,535| 0.219| | |School SES (ρ) | 6.1| 1,672| 0.126| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.1| 1,680| 0.139| 0.004| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.1| 1,675| 0.016| 0.523| |School (ICC) | 6.1| 1,685| 0.138| | |School SES (ρ) | 6.2| 596| 0.133| 0.001| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.2| 594| 0.080| 0.330| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.2| 596| 0.024| 0.551| |School (ICC) | 6.2| 596| 0.248| | |School SES (ρ) | 7.1| 759| 0.156| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.1| 802| 0.084| 0.235| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.1| 801| -0.003| 0.933| |School (ICC) | 7.1| 802| 0.127| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Verbal short-term memory” (codes 1942 and 522; DIS-ESP battery) assesses phonological short-term memory. The child selects a response among the options presented on the screen. It comprises 15 items. The time limit is 90 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013 and 2014 cohorts it was administered in 10 sessions, from 4 to 7 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .76 (N = 2,226, 15 items). Stability across successive administrations (median interval of 12 months) was ρ = .36 (median of 5 session pairs; range .23–.44). Stability across time points was ρ = .23–.44. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .56–.65. ## Pending issues - The task has 2 forms; in 2 of 2 comparisons they have different scales. Norms are given by form (see "Forms"). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
